s1.syndrome_frame: Progressive unsteadiness and recurrent falls with otologic abnormalities and osteolytic lesions
salient_findings: Progressive unsteadiness and recurrent falls over 5 days
Obstructed external ear canals with effusion and cerumen
Bilateral osteolysis of the mastoids and semicircular canals
key_facts: 4-year-old girl of Turkish ancestry
Progressive unsteadiness and recurrent falls over 5 days
Initial fall resulted in nasal bridge laceration
No prior medical history
Alert and afebrile on examination
External ear canals obstructed by effusion and cerumen
Three-month history of ear problems
Initial diagnosis of otitis media with effusion and tympanic perforation
Partial resolution with antibiotic treatment
Current otoscopic examination showed polypoid tissue and purulent secretion in right external canal
Contrast-enhanced CT showed bilateral osteolysis of mastoids and semicircular canals
Adenoid hypertrophy and mild sinus mucosal thickening on CT
Brainstem evoked response audiometry demonstrated profound right-sided hearing loss

shortlist.label: Langerhans cell histiocytosis
shortlist.why_kept: Bilateral osteolysis of mastoids and semicircular canals, otologic abnormalities, and osteolytic lesions are consistent with this diagnosis

shortlist.label: Cholesteatoma
shortlist.why_kept: Polypoid tissue and purulent secretion in the right external canal, and history of ear problems, are consistent with this diagnosis

shortlist.label: Osteomyelitis of the temporal bone
shortlist.why_kept: Osteolytic lesions and otologic abnormalities are consistent with this diagnosis, and the patient has a history of ear problems

shortlist.label: Mastoiditis
shortlist.why_kept: Osteolytic lesions and otologic abnormalities, including polypoid tissue and purulent secretion, are consistent with this diagnosis

shortlist.label: Erdheim-Chester disease
shortlist.why_kept: Bilateral osteolysis of mastoids and semicircular canals, and osteolytic lesions, are consistent with this rare diagnosis, although less likely than Langerhans cell histiocytosis

raw.rationale: The presence of bilateral osteolysis of the mastoids, superior and lateral semicircular canals, and the right external auditory canal, along with a separate osteolytic lesion in the dorsal left parietal bone, is highly suggestive of Langerhans cell histiocytosis, which is known to cause lytic bone lesions and can affect multiple sites, including the skull and temporal bones.

rejected.label: Cholesteatoma
rejected.why: While cholesteatoma can cause osteolysis, the presence of multiple osteolytic lesions and the involvement of the parietal bone are less typical for cholesteatoma.

rejected.label: Osteomyelitis of the temporal bone
rejected.why: Osteomyelitis could explain some of the findings, but the pattern of bilateral osteolysis and the separate parietal bone lesion are more suggestive of a systemic process like Langerhans cell histiocytosis.

rejected.label: Mastoiditis
rejected.why: Mastoiditis is a possible complication of otitis media, but it does not typically cause the widespread osteolysis seen in this case.

rejected.label: Erdheim-Chester disease
rejected.why: Erdheim-Chester disease is a rare form of histiocytosis that can cause bone lesions, but it is less common in children and the specific pattern of osteolysis in this case is more suggestive of Langerhans cell histiocytosis.
